title: 1 Samuel 27
paragraphs: ¹ David thought to himself, "One day Saul is going to kill me. The best thing I can do is escape to Philistine territory — then Saul will give up searching for me throughout Israel, and I'll be out of his reach." ² So David set out with his six hundred men and crossed over to Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath. ³ David and his men settled there with Achish in Gath, each man with his household. David had his two wives with him: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal. ⁴ When Saul learned that David had fled to Gath, he stopped searching for him. ⁵ David said to Achish, "If I have found favor with you, please give me a place in one of the country towns to live. There's no reason for your servant to live in the royal city with you."

⁶ So that day Achish gave him Ziklag, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since. ⁷ David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months. ⁸ During that time, David and his men raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites — peoples who had long lived in the land stretching toward Shur and Egypt. ⁹ Whenever David attacked a region, he left no one alive — no man or woman — and took their sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing. Then he would return to Achish. ¹⁰ Achish would ask, "Where did you raid today?" And David would say, "Against the Negev of Judah" or "Against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites" or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."

¹¹ David never left any man or woman alive to be brought back to Gath. He thought, "If we let them live, they might report what we've really been doing." This was his practice the whole time he lived in Philistine territory. ¹² Achish trusted David completely, thinking, "He's made himself so hated among his own people Israel that he'll be my servant forever."
